whatItDoes: Confirm the plumbing works before you build anything real. One step, `greet`, reads an optional name and returns a greeting — enough to prove build, deploy, and run end to end without spending anything or calling a capability.
longDescription:
The smallest valid Sapiom agent. It's a smoke test: use it to check that your setup builds, deploys, and runs before you reach for a template that actually does work.

There is one step. `greet` takes an optional `name`, and returns `{ greeting: "Hello, <name>!" }` — or `Hello, world!` if you leave the name out. That's the whole agent. It calls no capabilities and touches no external services.

Once this deploys and runs cleanly, you know the path works. From there, fork a capability-backed template like Web Research Digest and build the real thing on top of a foundation you've already seen work.

It makes no metered capability calls.
notes:
Click **Use this template** — Sapiom builds and deploys it for you; open it on the **Agents** page and run it.

The `name` input is optional: pass `{ "name": "Ada" }` to get `Hello, Ada!`, or run it with no input to get `Hello, world!`. The agent makes no metered capability calls.

Prefer to work from the code? Use `run_local` without signing in to execute the real step code on your machine. Because this template has no capabilities to stub, its agent logic and parsed input/output match the cloud path; the process environment is still local. Authenticate only when you are ready to link, deploy, or run in Sapiom cloud.

zeroSetup.narrative: Runs immediately with no setup and returns a greeting.
